lessons.title: Build a first draft
lessons.subtitle: Week 15: Producing and testing
lessons.body:
A first draft makes an idea reviewable. Use fictional inputs and mark uncertain details so reviewers can distinguish unfinished work from verified information.

Offline practice: Create the first version of your project artifact manually or with an optional online tool. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A first draft makes an idea reviewable. Use fictional inputs and mark uncertain details so reviewers can distinguish unfinished work from verified information.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
lessons.sourceName: UNESCO guidance on responsible AI in education

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains “Build a first draft”?
options: Every task requires training a new model.
A first draft makes an idea reviewable. Use fictional inputs and mark uncertain details so reviewers can distinguish unfinished work from verified information.
A polished AI answer is enough evidence that every claim is correct.
The human learner never needs to check the result.
questions.explanation: A first draft makes an idea reviewable. Use fictional inputs and mark uncertain details so reviewers can distinguish unfinished work from verified information.

questions.prompt: For the activity “Create the first version of your project artifact manually or with an optional online tool.”, which approach demonstrates learning?
options: Skip the activity and copy an unrelated answer.
Complete the activity, explain your reasoning, and record a limitation.
Share someone else’s private information to make the example realistic.
Treat an unverified generated response as final evidence.
questions.explanation: The activity asks you to apply this lesson. A written explanation and limitation make your understanding reviewable; a copied result alone does not.

questions.prompt: You return to the “Build a first draft” lesson after a break without internet. What can you do next?
options: Delete your previous work and start the whole course again.
Recall the key idea, check saved notes, and complete the offline activity.
Assume a cloud assistant will respond without a connection.
Wait until you can buy a paid AI subscription.
questions.explanation: The lesson and practice do not require an online tool. Retrieval and a small saved activity help you resume.

lessons.title: Test against the rubric
lessons.subtitle: Week 15: Producing and testing
lessons.body:

Offline practice: Score your first draft against your four criteria and explain each score. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

lessons.title: Test challenging examples
lessons.subtitle: Week 15: Producing and testing
lessons.body:
Challenging examples can reveal missing instructions, ambiguous wording, and unsuitable assumptions. Test both ordinary and unusual inputs relevant to the task.

Offline practice: Try one short input, one confusing input, and one incomplete input; record what failed. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

lessons.title: Revise and compare
lessons.subtitle: Week 15: Producing and testing
lessons.body:
A revision should address a recorded problem. Compare the revised version with the original using the same criteria and preserve both versions.

Offline practice: Make two specific corrections and show whether they improved your rubric results. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A revision should address a recorded problem. Compare the revised version with the original using the same criteria and preserve both versions.

lessons.title: Collect appropriate feedback
lessons.subtitle: Week 15: Producing and testing
lessons.body:
Feedback should address usefulness and clarity. Participation should be voluntary; avoid collecting unnecessary personal information or claiming a small sample proves broad impact.

Offline practice: Ask an available peer one clarity question, or complete a self-review if no peer is available. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: Feedback should address usefulness and clarity. Participation should be voluntary; avoid collecting unnecessary personal information or claiming a small sample proves broad impact.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
